headline: TALK ME DOWN — one sees the bomb, one holds the manual
lede: An original split-info co-op puzzle lands in the arcade: the defuser owns the panel but no rules, the manual-holder owns every rule but no hands. Shout across the couch — or press V and shout into the mic.

notes.text: TALK ME DOWN ships (#1252, PR #1304): NEON wire-cutting, DIAL-and-SET, and GLYPH sequence modules whose printed rules answer the stamps on the bomb — every rule a pure function of what the defuser can read aloud (serial digit, LED count, bolt color).

Solo you defuse while a CPU partner holds the manual and prints orders on the LCD rail; seat 2 joins the keyboard with the rulebook pages and a READ-N3 flagger. Voice is on from day one (#1247): heard calls pulse the right wire green or refuse with a why.

bombcheck 28 gates — rules-as-printed on 200 seeds, determinism, quota win 50/50 and slack (wins at 75% fuse); bombdrive 18/18 real-key browser runs x3; the fuse-tick mutant dies on cue. Also tonight: slot a merged SHORT ORDER SHOUT (#1248) — two co-op games in one night.

Slot etiquette lesson pinned: a claim script's 90-min liveness beat malformed checkpoint comments, but the open-PR + live-process reality check said yield — slot b yielded #1248 to slot a and took the next ladder rung instead of doubling a lane.
